messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: R novice trying to generate a figure for a publication
parts:
1) The PDF at that link isn't loading for me. Please don't make
everyone click through and hunt down the figure; better to copy it as
a small graphic and attach to your question, or just describe it.

2) You're posting this question to the ggplot2 listserv; I assume this
is what you want to use to make your plot? R has a number of plotting
packages.

3) If yes to #2, you're basically going to want to do the following
steps: import the data into R; transform it from 'wide' (multiple y
values per row) to 'long' (one y value per row); and plot.

4) Please read the link about reproducible examples that's given at
the bottom of all emails on this listserv.

5) In the spirit of reproducible examples, here's one that shows the
steps in #3 above:

df <- data.frame(x=1:2,group1=3:4,group2=5:6) # sample 'wide' data
library(reshape2)
df_long <- melt(df, id.vars=1) # melt to 'long' format
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df_long, aes(x,value))+geom_line(aes(color=variable)) # plot it

Ben

messages.subject: Re: R novice trying to generate a figure for a publication
parts:
Thanks for the image. Note that since you (again) didn't take the
trouble to provide a reproducible example or sample data, the
impression you're sending is that you expect people on this list to do
all your work for you. Which is not a great way to get help. However,
because I happened to have some time this morning, here's something to
get you started--hope it is useful.


library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw())

# Create sample data
df <- data.frame(obs=1:20,group=LETTERS[1:10], shading=1:2,
known=c(rep(T,10),rep(F,10)),score=runif(20))

# Set up the basic plot
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x=group, y=score))
p <- p + geom_blank() # not sure why I get an error without including this this

# Add background shading, alternating between groups
p <- p + geom_rect(aes(xmin=as.numeric(group)-0.5,xmax=as.numeric(group)+0.5,ymin=-Inf,ymax=Inf,fill=factor(shading)),
alpha=0.2)

# Add the points
p <- p + geom_point(aes(color=known))

# Fine-tune: custom colors, horizontal line, etc.
p <- p + scale_fill_grey(guide=F)
p <- p + scale_color_manual("", values=c("green", "yellow")) # point colors
p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept=0.5)

# Display and save the figure
print(p)
ggsave("sample.pdf")

Ben
